newsitem.title: LEBANON: Aoun supporters sentenced to jail in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Aoun supporters sentenced to jail in Lebanon.

text.p: A Lebanese military court on Thursday sentenced to jail 15 supporters of exiled Lebanese Christian leader and former army commander General Michel Aoun on charges related to state security, judicial sources said.

They said the court found the Christians guilty of distributing leaflets that "weaken security, provoke sectarian strife, incite riots and mutiny and disturb Lebanon's relations with a neighbouring country".
This was an apparent reference to Syria, which has 35,000 troops in Lebanon and is the country's main power broker.

Thirteen men and women were sentenced to between 10 days and one month imprisonment. They included the treasurer of the Lebanese engineers union. They can appeal the rulings to a higher military court.
A 14th suspect was sentenced to three months in absentia and another to one year in absentia. If they surrender or are arrested, they will be retried.

Aoun, a Maronite Christian, has lived in exile in France since 1991 after leading an ill-fated attempt to drive Syrian forces from Lebanon. It ended when his units were crushed by the Syrians in Beirut in October 1990.
